payload.reason: The evidence indicates a correlation between daytime activity and socioeconomic status, suggesting that people active during the day tend to have higher socioeconomic status and use more standard language.

claims.text: People active during the daytime are more likely to use standard language compared to those active at night, indicating a correlation with socioeconomic status.
Higher socioeconomic status is associated with daytime activity on Twitter, as those tweeting during the day have higher average incomes.
Temporal activity influences linguistic variability, with standard language usage peaking during the day due to the socioeconomic composition of active users.
